title: What happens when a label prints
summary: One request, POST /orders/:id/ship, followed from the route to the event consumer across three files. Explanatory: no questions.

blocks.title: Ship an order
blocks.entry: POST /orders/:id/ship, called by the warehouse label printer

steps.title: The route parses the id and calls the worker
steps.summary: No auth check here; the printer's token is checked by middleware one layer up.
steps.detail: `Number()` turns a bad id into `NaN`, which the worker then looks up and reports as not found. Fine, but the 404 hides a malformed request.

steps.title: Load the order
steps.code:
const order = await db.orders.get(orderId)
if (!order) throw new NotFound(orderId)

steps.title: Not found
steps.summary: Thrown to the route, which maps it to a 404.

steps.title: Cancelled orders are left alone
steps.summary: The guard runs before the write, but not atomically with it.
warnings: A cancellation between this line and the update still gets the flag. This is the race the fulfillment review fixes.

steps.title: Set the flag
steps.summary: Writes `shipped = true`; nothing checks that status still allows it.

steps.title: Emit order.shipped
steps.summary: Fire and forget; consumers run out of band.

steps.title: The notifier sends the email
steps.summary: Reads the order again, so a cancelled order can still get a shipped email.
steps.detail: The consumer trusts the event. Once the status transition refuses `cancelled → shipped`, this path goes quiet for cancelled orders with no change here.

steps.title: Return the order to the route
steps.summary: The spread copies the row with the flag set, whether or not the write happened.
warnings: On the cancelled branch the function returns the row unchanged, but on the happy path it returns `shipped: true` without re-reading, so a concurrent cancel is invisible to the caller.
